Messages.Author: Matthew Farney
Messages.Body:
Yes Ramses III's Tomb is cool. ;)

Here's some I liked in my packs:
Memory's Fading Glimpse (3 vamp blood & Obfuscate) Directed. Move a
vampire from your prey's inactive region to the bottom of his/her crypt.
Move all of the blood on that vampire to your prey's blood pool. Bold:
As above, but move on blood from the inactive vampire to the acting
vampire.

Lure of the Serpent: (1 vamp blood & Serpentis) Directed. The acting
vampire takes control of a retainer controlled by another vampire.
Bold: Take control of an ally controlled by another methuselah.

Uncontrollable Rage [Reaction] (2 vamp & Protean) Only usable when the
acting vampire's action is announced. This acting minion get +1 agg.
hand damage until the end of this action. Bold: +2

The Death of My Consciense [Combat] (3 vamp & Potence) Requires a
vampire with capacity above 5. Do not replace until after combat.
After range has been chosen, burn up to 4 cards in you hand. For each
card you burn this way, the vampire gets +1 hand damage for the
remainder of the combat. Do not replace these cards until after combat.
Bold: As above, with +2

I'm not sure, but the above are all uncommon/rare I think. THe commons
seemed to be in the front of the packs. *shrug*

I do like this one for one of my decks. :)
Alacrity. Celerity and 2 vamp.
+1 stealth. Bold: As above and if blocked, gain an optional manuever in
first round of combat. Fits in a Torrie bleed deck well. :) Specially
with some of the other cards. ;)

-Matt

Messages.Author: Woody Carey
Messages.Body:
On 2 Jun 1996, Matthew Farney wrote:

> The Death of My Consciense [Combat] (3 vamp & Potence) Requires a
> vampire with capacity above 5. Do not replace until after combat.
> After range has been chosen, burn up to 4 cards in you hand. For each
> card you burn this way, the vampire gets +1 hand damage for the
> remainder of the combat. Do not replace these cards until after combat.
> Bold: As above, with +2

Although a vampire with superior potence could in theory take down and IC
vampire with this card in combo with a Torn Signpost, I didn't find it that
useful, and for the following reasons:
1. You have to pitch cards to get the bonus. I don't about the rest of
you, but I run my decks so tight that every card in my hand is useful and
not really "ho-hum, pitch it" material.
2.All this blustering of cards and damage can sidestepped with a simple
dodge or combat ends and you've just whizzed away good cards from your hand.

Sure combat decks tend to like to cycle cards, but the benefits of this
card were marginal at best as I saw it used all night last night. Any
other opinions on this one?

Messages.Body:
Woody Carey <wca...@gladstone.uoregon.edu> writes:





The modifiers do *not* go away when an action is blocked.
Stealth still hangs around (in the event the action gets continued).

Some modifiers only apply to blocked actions (Dawn Op, Alacrity, etc.)

Alacrity (Cel:2: +1 stealth *As above and this vampire gets an optional
maneuevr in the first round of combat if the action is blocked) would
be pretty silly if it didn't apply to a blocked action.

The whole point of using a Bum's Rush with Uncontrollable Rage is to
ensure that you get into combat. Few people would block a bleed from
a gangrel (who don't normally bleed for much) when they know that the
Gangrel is going to be punching for 2 agg. This way - they block the Rush
or they don't - someone still gets slapped for 2 agg (unless combat
is ended or he strike is dodged or the "victim" maneuvers away, etc).

Messages.Author: The Corrupter
Messages.Body:
On Wed, 5 Jun 1996, Daniel Hoffman wrote:

[Re: Death of My Conscience being useful or no]

> I still think Torn Signpost, Undead Strength for 5 and 1 FoD for 7, 2
> for 9 or 3 for 11 is a better way to go. All the cards are replaced and
> you only spend as much blood as you really need. The only thing is FoD
> is rare. I'll stick with blurred signposts for 9, thank you.

Death of my Conscience has one huge thing going for it: No need for a
combo.

While Torn Signpost, Undead Strength, Fists of Death can give you 3 cards
for 5 or 7 damage and only 1 blood, DoMC can do, for one card, up to +8
damage per strike. Yes, the blood cost is more, the cards are not
replaced, and only old vampires can use it, but DoMC need not have all of
the cards show up at once to be damaging. DoMC and even a Nimble Feet
are disgusting.

One thing I think DoMC really combats is the horribly strong Ravnos
combat deck (no joke) loaded with Trap, Drawing out the Beast, and
Apparations (along with other minor damage prevention). When you have
Ravnos Trapping and preventing 6 damage each round, things get ugly.

I think the advantage of DoMC is not that it's that awesome a combat card
but that it allows you to discard cards you can't use, or can't use now.
If you have 4 masters in your hand at the beginning of the turn, ditching
all, or all but one of them, will help you a lot even if you get no other
